public_rationale: The forecast that more power would not be available for a year or more is contradicted on the plain, site-wide reading. Epoch AI wrote that an Oracle post implied only 200MW was operational at Abilene as of April 22, 2026 (e1). That fits his 'around 200MW', but it is six weeks after his March 10 post. On June 11, 2026, The Next Web reported that Oracle had delivered 42% of Abilene's capacity (e2). A tracker reports that on its September 10, 2026 earnings call, Oracle said six of eight buildings had been delivered (e3). Oracle put that at 618MW and 75% of the campus. It also said it delivered 131,000 GPUs at Abilene during the quarter (e3). This is substantially more than about 200MW, well before March 10, 2027, so it meets the contract's early-resolution rule. A summary of The Information's report says OpenAI passed on six additional buildings because power would not be available for roughly a year (e4). Under that narrower reading, the forecast would not be due until about March 2027.
limitations: 'Delivered' capacity is Oracle's measure and may not equal energized power.
The September figures come from a tracker quoting Oracle's call. The transcript was not read directly.
The Information's article was not read. Its scope is known only from a secondary summary.
The evidence does not directly measure operating power in March 2026, when he wrote the post.
Under the narrower expansion-only reading, the forecast is not yet testable.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Stargate Abilene currently has only around 200MW of power, and, as The Information reports and he said in October, more power won't be available for a year or more.
conditions: citing The Information and his own October reporting

statement.excerpt: As I reported back in October, Stargate currently only has around 200MW of power, and The Information reports that power won’t be available for a year or more, something I also said in October.

from_speaker: Stargate currently only has around 200MW of power
The Information reports that power won't be available for a year or more
our_interpretation: Part 1 (current state): in March 2026 Stargate Abilene had only about 200MW operating.
Part 2 (forecast): plain reading is that more power at Abilene, beyond about 200MW, would not be available for at least a year after the post, i.e., not before about March 10, 2027.

The Information's report, as summarized elsewhere, was about power for six additional expansion buildings. A reader of his sentence would take it to mean the Stargate site as a whole, so I use that plain reading and flag the difference.
criteria.support_condition: About 200MW operating around March 2026, and no meaningful added power at Abilene before about March 2027.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Abilene had much more than 200MW in March 2026, or substantially more power came online there before March 2027.

evidence.excerpt: a subsequent post by Oracle implied that only 200 megawatts (or about 0.3 GW of total facility power by our estimate) was operational as of April 22nd.
evidence.explanation: Supports the first part: around the time of the post, Abilene had only about 200MW operating.

evidence.excerpt: The company has delivered 42% of capacity at its flagship Stargate site in Abilene, Texas
evidence.locator: section OpenAI and the Abilene campus
evidence.explanation: By June 2026, three months after the post, 42% of the 1.2 GW campus (about 500MW) was delivered, well above 200MW.

evidence.excerpt: Oracle said six of the eight buildings, representing 618 megawatts and 75 percent of the campus, had been delivered, that it delivered 131,000 GPUs at Abilene during the quarter
evidence.explanation: Six months after the post, Oracle reported 618MW across six buildings delivered, with GPUs installed. That is about three times the 200MW, well before the one-year mark.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI passed on six additional buildings because power will not be available for roughly a year.
evidence.explanation: The Information's one-year delay apparently concerned power for six extra expansion buildings, not the existing campus. Under that narrower reading the forecast is not yet due.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: Before March 10, 2027, Oracle reported 618MW across six of eight Abilene buildings as delivered. This is substantially more than about 200MW, which meets the rule that such a report contradicts the forecast.
